findings.title: Immortal time bias and lack of active-comparator/new-user design
findings.mechanism: Classifying exposure as 'any prior or current use' without a new-user design, washout period, or time-to-event analysis creates immortal person-time and misclassifies unexposed person-time prior to drug initiation as exposed, artificially lowering the event rate in the exposed arm.
findings.direction: Pushes the estimate toward a protective effect (lower OR), as patients must survive event-free until their first prescription to enter the exposed cohort. The observed event rate in GLP-1 is lower (1.62% vs 2.47% full, 1.62% vs 2.31% matched).
evidence: Exposure defined as 'Любое prior или current использование'
No minimum treatment duration or washout period
Time-to-event analysis was not performed; static logistic regression used

findings.title: Failure to exclude or match on prior breast cancer history and comorbidities
findings.mechanism: Patients with active, severe, or prior cancer are systematically less likely to be prescribed newly initiated metabolic drugs like GLP-1 agonists (contraindication or prioritization of oncology care), while the control group may include patients with past history or higher unmeasured baseline oncologic risk.
findings.direction: Pushes the estimate toward a protective effect for GLP-1, evidenced by the lower baseline event rate in GLP-1 users (247 / 15,264 = 1.62% vs 353 / 15,264 = 2.31% in matched controls).
evidence: Matching explicitly omitted 'истории рака груди, коморбидности'
No explicit exclusion criterion for pre-existing breast cancer prior to cohort entry

findings.title: Biologically implausible latency period for solid tumor prevention
findings.mechanism: The observation window is only 3.5 years (Jan 2022 – Jun 2025) with no minimum exposure requirement. Carcinogenesis and detectable breast tumor development operate on multi-year to decadal timelines; an immediate reduction in cancer incidence reflects detection/selection dynamics rather than biological cancer prevention.
findings.direction: Pushes toward an exaggerated protective association (OR 0.695 in matched cohort) that cannot biologically reflect incident tumor prevention over a maximum of 3.5 years.
evidence: Observation period: 1 января 2022 — 30 июня 2025 (3.5 years)
No minimum duration of GLP-1 therapy required

findings.title: Conditioning on post-baseline or distortive metric (Maximum BMI)
findings.mechanism: Matching on 'maximum BMI' rather than baseline BMI or weight trajectory can induce collider bias or misalign metabolic severity between groups, failing to control for actual obesity exposure duration and weight loss dynamics.
findings.direction: Unclear/residual confounding in favor of healthier or different metabolic profiles in GLP-1 users.
evidence: Matched on 'максимальный BMI' rather than baseline BMI
Not matched on 'динамике веса'

findings.title: Conditioning on post-exposure screening mammography and selection bias
findings.mechanism: The study restricts the starting population exclusively to women who underwent mammography. If GLP-1 users have different healthcare-seeking behaviors, screening intervals, or indications for mammography compared to non-users, conditioning on screening creates collider or selection bias. Furthermore, screening frequency and regularity were not matched between groups.
findings.direction: Pushes the estimate toward a lower observed odds ratio (apparent protective effect, OR 0.695), as the GLP-1 group had a lower detection proportion among screened individuals (1.62% vs 2.31% in matched controls).
evidence: Starting cohort defined strictly by mammography: 217,624 women
Screen-detected cases constituted 241/247 (97.6%) of GLP-1 cancers and 2,295/2,381 (96.4%) of control cancers
Mammography frequency and regularity were excluded from matching variables

findings.title: Immortal time bias, lack of latency period, and undefined exposure duration
findings.mechanism: Exposure was defined as any prior or current GLP-1 prescription before the cutoff date with no requirement for minimum therapy duration, dosage threshold, or washout period. Cancer development involves multi-year biological latency; counting any single prescription prior to diagnosis without a washout or induction window artificially misclassifies short/recent exposure as protective and allows immortal time to accrue.
findings.direction: Biases toward an exaggerated protective effect (OR 0.695), because patients who develop cancer quickly after baseline without starting GLP-1 or with very brief exposure are assigned to control or credited to GLP-1 without sufficient biological time for drug-mediated antineoplastic action.
evidence: Exposure defined as 'any prior or current GLP-1 prescription; first prescription prior to cutoff date'
No minimum duration of therapy required, dosage not accounted for, no washout period
No time-to-event or hazard ratio analysis conducted; evaluated via cross-sectional 2x2 contingency tables and logistic regression

findings.title: Residual and intermediate confounding via maximal BMI and unadjusted weight dynamics
findings.mechanism: Matching used 'maximal BMI over 2017–2025' rather than baseline BMI at the time of drug initiation. Maximal BMI during the follow-up window post-exposure is a post-baseline mediator/intermediate variable affected by GLP-1 weight loss, and weight trajectories were not matched. Additionally, breast cancer history and overall comorbidity were omitted from matching.
findings.direction: Distorts the effect estimate in favor of an apparent protective effect (OR 0.695 in matched cohort), by inadequately adjusting for pre-treatment metabolic risk and conditioning on a post-treatment maximum BMI.
evidence: Matching used maximal BMI (2017-2025)
Matching did NOT adjust for history of breast cancer, comorbidity, or weight trajectory
Control group was artificially enriched with diabetes (17.6% to 53.4%) during 1:1 matching to match GLP-1 group

findings.title: Internal reporting discrepancy in cohort accounting
findings.mechanism: Discrepancy in the reported baseline cohort size indicates potential data processing or record accounting errors in the study cascade.
findings.direction: Unclear numerical direction; reflects internal documentation inconsistency.
evidence: Abstract reports starting cohort as 217,025
Results section and Figure 1 report starting cohort as 217,624 (discrepancy of 599 individuals)

findings.title: Baseline breast cancer history imbalance (Prevalent disease / Prior history confounding)
findings.mechanism: Patients with a prior history of breast cancer are at a substantially higher risk of a subsequent or recurrent breast cancer diagnosis. Matching explicitly omitted history of breast cancer, resulting in a higher proportion of baseline breast cancer in the control group compared to the GLP-1 group.
findings.direction: Pushes the odds ratio below 1.0 (spuriously favors GLP-1 / protective effect), because the control group has a higher baseline prevalence of prior breast cancer (7.8% matched, 9.2% full) compared to the GLP-1 group (5.9%).
evidence: Matched cohort personal history of breast cancer: Control 7.8% vs GLP-1 5.9%
Full cohort personal history of breast cancer: Control 9.2% (8,876 women) vs GLP-1 5.9% (907 women)
Matching was explicitly NOT performed on breast cancer history

findings.title: Immortal time bias and lack of time-to-event analysis (Pervasive exposure misclassification)
findings.mechanism: Exposure was defined as any prior or current prescription before cutoff with no minimum duration, no dose consideration, and no washout period. Evaluating time-invariant binary exposure in logistic regression without time-to-event accounting creates immortal time bias and includes prevalent users.
findings.direction: Pushes the odds ratio below 1.0 (spuriously favors GLP-1 / protective effect), as patients had to survive and remain cancer-free long enough to receive a prescription, misclassifying unexposed person-time prior to GLP-1 initiation.

No minimum duration required, dose ignored, no washout period
Time-to-event analysis was not performed; logistic regression evaluated binary outcome over 2022-2025

findings.title: Selection / Indication bias from matching on maximum BMI rather than baseline BMI
findings.mechanism: Matching on maximum BMI rather than pre-treatment baseline BMI or weight trajectory can induce collider bias or mask differential weight loss/gain patterns, while the GLP-1 group has substantially higher baseline multi-morbidity indicating severe metabolic indication.
findings.direction: Unclear net direction on incidence directly, but distorts comparative baseline risk profile between groups.
